- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average for stabilization.
- If sentiment is positive (≥0.4) and price is trending up, model often overreacts; apply downward bias of 1–2% to avoid overconfidence in momentum.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.1–0.3), model exhibits mean-reversion bias — forecast tends to be too high; apply 1–2% downward adjustment to align with recent mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently fails to capture short-term volatility; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% recent, 30% sentiment) to reduce overfitting to recent trends.
- If sentiment drops sharply after a peak, model often ignores the reversal; add a 2–4% downward correction to reflect sentiment shift.
- Avoid forecasting when sentiment is below 0.1 for 3+ consecutive days — model tends to be overly optimistic; use 0.05–0.15 as floor for price forecasts.
